class.name: NetwProbeResult
class.brief_description: Categorical outcome of a server probe.

method.name: busy
method.description: Returns a [constant STATUS_BUSY] result carrying [param message]. The server answered and refused: it is full, or the probe arrived outside its rate window.

method.name: error
method.description: Returns a [constant STATUS_ERROR] result carrying [param message]. The probe itself went wrong, rather than the server answering something.

method.name: incompatible
method.description: Returns a [constant STATUS_INCOMPATIBLE] result carrying [param message]. The server answered with a [member NetwServerInfo.app_id] or [member NetwServerInfo.version] this build cannot join, so [param info] is kept: a browser row still has something to show even though the join would be refused.

method.name: is_ok
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when [member status] is [constant STATUS_OK], which is the one status that says the server answered and this build may join it.

method.name: ok
method.description: Returns a [constant STATUS_OK] result advertising [param info], measured at [param latency_ms]. A result discovered through a lobby directory rather than a round trip passes [code]-1[/code], which is how [NetwServerBrowser] marks a row it has no ping for.

method.name: timeout
method.description: Returns a [constant STATUS_TIMEOUT] result carrying [param message]. The probe reached the wire and nothing came back inside the window.

method.name: unreachable
method.description: Returns a [constant STATUS_UNREACHABLE] result carrying [param message]. The connection or the peer authentication failed before any server reply.

method.name: unsupported
method.description: Returns a [constant STATUS_UNSUPPORTED] result. This is what a [NetwTransport] answers when it has no cheap way to ask, so a caller reads it as "unknown", never as "down".

members.member: What the server advertised about itself, or [code]null[/code] when it never answered. Carried by [constant STATUS_OK] and [constant STATUS_INCOMPATIBLE], and by nothing else.
The probe round trip in milliseconds, or [code]-1[/code] when the result came from a directory listing instead of a round trip. Meaningful only under [constant STATUS_OK].
Diagnostic detail about why the probe ended the way it did. It names the failing step for a log, so it is not player-facing text.
The outcome category, and the member every caller branches on. It defaults to [constant STATUS_UNSUPPORTED], so a bare [code]new()[/code] reads as "nothing was asked" rather than as a failure.

constants.constant: The server answered and this build may join it. [method is_ok] tests for exactly this.
The connection or the peer authentication failed before the server replied.
Nothing came back inside the probe window.
The transport cannot probe, so the server's state is unknown rather than bad.
The server answered and refused, being full or rate limiting probes.
The probe itself failed, with [member message] naming the step.
The server answered with a build this client cannot join, and [member info] survives so a row can still be rendered.
